title: Annotatio IV §.VII cont.: De Resurrectione Carnis nearly corporal — counted among his errors
pass_a_gloss: Although the same Tertullian elsewhere, namely in the Book on the Resurrection of the Flesh, is also read to have inculcated a nearly corporal presence of Christ’s body in the Eucharist, writing: Our flesh is fed with the body and blood of Christ, that the soul also may be fattened from God: Which is to be numbered among the other errors of this Father, otherwise rightly venerable, or among those known to the learned public, for even the Transsubstantiators themselves wholly abhor a properly so-called nutrition of our flesh by Christ’s body taken in the Sacred supper, as we said above.
pass_b_english: Elsewhere (De Resurrectione Carnis) Tertullian seems to push a nearly corporal presence: our flesh is fed with Christ’s body and blood so the soul may be fattened from God.
Count that among his otherwise venerable errors — even Transsubstantiators wholly abhor proper nutrition of our flesh by Christ’s body taken in the supper.
source_text: Quanquam Idem Tertullianus, alibi, nempe Libro de Resurrectione Carnis, etiam præsentiam corporis Christi in Eucharistia ferè corporalem inculcasse legatur, scribens: Caro (nostra) corpore & sanguine Christi vescitur, ut & anima de Deo saginetur: Id quod ceteris Patris hujus, jure alioquin venerandi, erroribus, vel in vulgus eruditorum notis, annumerandum eô fuerit, quia vel ipsi Transsubstantiatores, à nutritione carnis nostræ propriè dicta per corpus Christi, in S. cœna sumtum, omninò abhorrent, ut suprà diximus.
notes: Nearly corporal error; Transsubst. also reject.
